title: K Closest Points to Origin
statement: Given a list of points `[x, y]` and an integer `k`, return the `k` points closest to the origin (0, 0). The answer may be in any order.

example.why: Squared distances are 18, 26, 20 and 2, so the two closest points are (1, 1) and (3, 3).

idea: The distance from (x, y) to the origin is √(x² + y²). To *compare* distances the square root is not needed: x² + y² orders the points the same way.
We need the k smallest distances, not a full sort.
Put every (distance, point) pair in a **min-heap** and pop k times. Each pop hands back the closest point that is still left.

complexity.timeWhy: Heapify is O(n); each of the k pops costs O(log n).

steps.text: Our example: **`points = [[3,3],[5,-1],[-2,4],[1,1]], k = 2`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
For every point compute x² + y² — the squared distance to the origin — and pair it with the point: [18, 26, 20, 2].
Heapify: the pair with the **smallest distance** is now on top.
Pop the closest point that is still in the heap: **(1, 1)**, at squared distance 2.
Pop the closest point that is still in the heap: **(3, 3)**, at squared distance 18.
After 2 pops we have the 2 closest points: **[[1, 1], [3, 3]]**.
Done — the answer is **`[[1,1],[3,3]]`**. Squared distances are 18, 26, 20 and 2, so the two closest points are (1, 1) and (3, 3).
